sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. Sec.2.1.1: contrastive vowel length (verbs: first root syllable only), automatic lengthening before NC and after glides, 'intonational lengthening' mentioned but not marked; sec.2.3 Tone: H/zero (or L/zero per Hyman) system, high-tone anticipation, toneless syllables after the last H extra-low 'making the H tone perceptually prominent'. No statement of word-level stress.

sources.citation: Crane, Thera Marie. 2011. Beyond Time: Temporal and Extra-temporal Functions of Tense and Aspect Marking in Totela, a Bantu Language of Zambia. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. 423 pp. (author's web copy via the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent. Ch.2 sec.2.2.4 (pp.70-71): five vowels with contrastive length, 'although the role of length may be diminishing'; notes other Bantu Botatwe languages lack contrastive length and 'penultimate lengthening may instead be found' there; sec.2.2.5 and Appendix C (pp.369ff): tone system H(/L or zero), four surface tones H, !H, L, HL, regular high-tone anticipation, phrase-final super-low L after last H. No use of 'stress'/'accent' for Totela anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).
